subject: Re: Post-call: caching assumptions & pricing (hit rate estimates)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@fastretail.com>; Taylor Chen <taylor.chen@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & ask: caching hit rates + target $/1M tokens

Thanks again for the time this morning — quick recap and the two items we need to finalize pricing and the MAP.

Recap (short):
- Use case: customer support assistant + product search reranking (mixed generate + embed lookups).
- Expected traffic: bursty during peak shopping hours; need predictable monthly spend and SLA for Dedicated.
- Key procurement asks: target unit economics ($/1M tokens), token volumes, and any prefix/response reuse expectations.

What we need from you to finalize numbers:
1) Ballpark monthly token volume (1M tokens = useful unit) — uplifts are ok (e.g., 10–50M / 50–200M).
2) Target billable $/1M tokens or budget range you’re targeting for production.
3) Any existing caching or reuse expectations (do you expect 20–60% prefix reuse for repeated prompts; are prompts highly templated?).

Suggested assumptions from our side (see attached Excel):
- Base service unit cost: $12 / 1M tokens (list price for this proposal varies with committed monthly volume).
- Prefix cache strategy: assume a 40% prefix-hit-rate for templated prompts (helps reduce effective downstream generation tokens).
- Effective cost math: Effective $/1M tokens = base $/1M * (1 - cache_hit_rate) — i.e., if 40% hit, effective cost = $12 * 0.6 = $7.2 / 1M tokens.

Next steps: please reply with items 1–3 above. If it helps, we can run a short 1-week traffic capture / sample to measure real hit rate before we finalize pricing.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@fastretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Taylor Chen <taylor.chen@fastretail.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & ask: caching hit rates + target $/1M tokens

Appreciate the clear notes — answers below:

1) Monthly token volume (expected):
- Pilot (Q2): 25–40M tokens / month.
- Production (Q4 target): 300–500M tokens / month (depending on rollout).

2) Budget range / target billable rate:
- Procurement is targeting blended spend of ~$6k-$10k/month for the pilot. For production, leadership is modeling operational costs and wants an effective $/1M tokens around $8–$10 if possible.

3) Caching / reuse expectations:
- Prompts are moderately templated. We expect prefix reuse on the assistant flows roughly 30–45% (users hit similar system+instruction + entity slots). For product search reranks, reuse is lower (~10–20%).

We can provide a 7-day sample of anonymized prompt traces for you (stripped of PII) — will need an NDA addendum if that’s required. Also happy to have your team do a quick runbook to estimate hit rate from our logs.

— Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of ML, FastRetail Inc.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Taylor Chen <taylor.chen@fastretail.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & ask: caching hit rates + target $/1M tokens

Thanks Alex — that range is super helpful. I ran quick sensitivity calcs based on your estimates and our standard prefix-cache model to show effective $/1M tokens under different hit rates. See the numbers below (also in attached sheet):

Assumptions we used for the table:
- Base proposed list price (example for Dedicated commitment): $12 / 1M tokens (you’ll get improved unit pricing on a larger commit).
- We separate two traffic buckets: 
  * Assistant flows (templated): assume hit rates between 30–45%.
  * Rerank flows (low reuse): assume hit rates 10–20%.
- Weighted mix for pilot: 70% assistant, 30% rerank (you can change mix).

Examples (pilot mix 70/30):
- Case A (conservative): assistant hit 30%, rerank 10% -> aggregate hit = 0.7*0.3 + 0.3*0.1 = 0.24 (24%) -> effective factor = 0.76 -> effective $/1M = $12 * 0.76 = $9.12
- Case B (mid): assistant 40%, rerank 15% -> agg hit = 0.7*0.4 + 0.3*0.15 = 0.325 -> eff factor = 0.675 -> effective $/1M = $12 * 0.675 = $8.10
- Case C (optimistic): assistant 45%, rerank 20% -> agg hit = 0.7*0.45 + 0.3*0.2 = 0.355 -> eff factor = 0.645 -> effective $/1M = $12 * 0.645 = $7.74

Mapping to your budget targets:
- Pilot tokens 25–40M / month: at $9.12 / 1M (Case A) that’s ~$228–$365 / month billable (note: this is illustrative — committed minimums and platform/throughput fees apply).
- Production 300–500M / month: with a volume discount we can push base to $9 / 1M; with similar hit rates effective could be ~$5.8–$6.5 / 1M which aligns with your $8–$10 leadership target. We’ll size discounts in the MAP.

Notes / open items:
- We recommend running the 7-day sample to measure your real prefix reuse; our sales engineering team (Marcus) can run the hit-rate calc and return a tightened estimate.
- Also worth measuring sequence length distributions — longer generations increase tokens per request and change unit economics.

Next steps I propose:
1) You send the anonymized sample (or we provide a lightweight capture script).
2) Marcus and I will produce a short hit-rate + cost sensitivity appendix and update the MAP with proposed committed tiers.
3) We’ll schedule a 30-min technical workshop to align on capture and SLA targets.

I’ve attached the Excel with the above calcs and a preliminary MAP draft. Let us know preferred times for the workshop.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Adding for SEM/SE next steps — happy to run the sample and produce a short appendix. My proposed deliverables:
- 7-day hit-rate analysis (by flow) + recommendation on prefix cache keying strategy.
- Effective $/1M sensitivity table (we’ll include a few base pricing tiers: $12 / $9 / $7 per 1M pre-cache).
- Short notes on how batching/kv-cache and quantization could further lower your effective spend (qualitative).

If you can share the sample by COB Friday PDT we’ll have the appendix back early next week. I’ve attached the capture template we usually use.

Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
